note: Hand-derived oracle for recipe-problems.plynal: every recipe check a saved recipe can give (step 22's notation is 207 characters, past the 200 Ply reads) except empty-recipe (recipe-empty) and too-large (a file past the limits is refused as unreadable; unit tests cover it). The quoted notation messages are the notation reader's own words (rust/ply-nalbind/src/notation.rs); everything else is derived by hand from the rules. Part 1 is steps 2 to 7, Part 2 steps 9 to 18, Part 3 steps 19 to 25; refused steps leave the count where it was (10 in Part 2).

segments.written: Work in a spiral for 3 rounds.
Make a foundation chain of 0 stitches and join it into a ring.
Work in rounds for 4 rounds.
Work back and forth in rows until there are 10 stitches.
Increase 2 stitches in each round for 3 rounds.
Decrease 0 stitches in each round for 2 rounds.
Finish.
Work 2 short rows back and forth over part of the round.
Start in the round at the centre with 10 stitches.
Decrease 3 stitches in each round, skipping a loop of the previous round, for 4 rounds.
Decrease 1 stitch in each round until 12 stitches remain.
Increase until there are 10 stitches.
Increase 1,000,001 stitches in each round for 1 round.
Leave an opening: skip 10 loops of the previous round and work 4 stitches across the gap without connecting them.
Leave an opening: skip 2 loops of the previous round and work 2 stitches across the gap without connecting them.
Join the edges of an opening to close it.
Join the edges of the opening in step 15 (Gap) to close it.
Leave an opening.
Pick up loops around the opening in step 15 (Gap) to start this part.
Join the edges of an opening to close it.
Join the edges of an opening to close it.
Work in joined rounds until a point the recipe does not state.
Work back and forth in rows until it measures -3 cm (from the pick-up).
Work in rounds for 2 rounds.

issues.text: Step 1 (Too early): comes before any start: begin the recipe with a start (a foundation chain, a centre start, or loops picked up from earlier work)
Step 2 (Ring): makes a foundation chain of 0 stitches: a count must be at least 1
Step 3 (Cuff): the stitch has no connection to the previous round (such as F1 or B1), so the recipe does not say how this step joins the round before
Step 4 (No id): has no id, so no other step can name it
Step 4 (No id): works until a number of stitches, but only an increase or a decrease changes the stitch count
Step 5 (Twin): has the same id (segment-1) as step 1 (Too early), so a step that names it is ambiguous

Step 5 (Twin): the stitch notation has a problem at "+1": `+1` uses the `+` dialect (as in `F1+1`, or the `a+b` thumb-loop alias), which is not Hansen notation and is not interpreted; kept verbatim in the extra text of connection `F1`
Step 6 (Bad notation): the stitch notation has a problem at "F999": connection count 999 is out of range (0 to 255); the structure holds 255 and the written count is kept only in the source text
Step 6 (Bad notation): decreases by 0 stitches: a count must be at least 1
Step 8 (After the end): comes after Part 1 was finished in step 7 (Edge): begin the next part with a start (a foundation chain, a centre start, or loops picked up from earlier work)
Step 9 (Second part): the target measurement gives 4 with no unit: choose mm, cm or in
Step 10 (Too many off): removes 12 stitches (3 in each of 4 rounds), but the round has only 10
Step 11 (Down to more): decreases until there are 12 stitches, but the round has only 10
Step 12 (Up to fewer): increases until there are 10 stitches, but the round already has 10
Step 13 (Huge): increases by 1,000,001 stitches, more than Ply counts (1,000,000)
Step 14 (Wide gap): skips 10 loops of the previous round, but the round has only 10: an opening must leave part of the round connected
Step 14 (Wide gap): this opening is never worked or closed: add a pick-up that starts from it, or a join that closes it
Step 16 (Close early): closes the opening in step 18 (Vague gap), which comes later: an opening can only be worked or closed after the step that makes it
Step 18 (Vague gap): this step does not say both how many loops it skips and how many stitches it works across the gap, so the stitches after it cannot be counted; later counts are not checked
Step 18 (Vague gap): Part 2 ends here without a finish: add a finish step after this one
Step 18 (Vague gap): this opening is never worked or closed: add a pick-up that starts from it, or a join that closes it
Step 19 (Third part): starts from the opening in step 15 (Gap), but step 17 (Close the gap) already closed it
Step 20 (Not a gap): closes step 9 (Second part), which is not an opening
Step 21 (Lost): closes a step that is not in the recipe (segment-99)
Step 22 (Until when): the stitch notation is longer than 200 characters, so Ply does not read it
Step 22 (Until when): works until a point the recipe does not state: name a landmark (such as the base of the thumb) or give a measurement
Step 23 (Negative): the measurement it works until is -3 cm, but a length must be more than 0
Step 24 (Blank): has no text
Step 25 (Which stitch): is set to its own stitch, but no notation is given
Step 25 (Which stitch): Part 3 ends here without a finish: add a finish step after this one
Fit 1 (Hand around): this measurement has no value yet
